headline: High-risk default overlap: ms-swift can write files and use broad network while opik ingests via REST, creating leakage and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, while opik exposes a REST API. A plausible bridge is file- or output-based handoff where opik consumes ms-swift-generated content as trusted input. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF opik ingests ms-swift output from a shared file or pasted transcript without sanitization
IF an operator routes ms-swift-generated text into opik prompts or evaluation payloads
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any ms-swift output is forwarded to opik
Use separate directories for ms-swift artifacts and opik inputs
Strip instructions and markup from transferred text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoff files

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift explicitly touches secrets-like hub_token/sdk-token and writes files; opik has broad network egress and REST API access. If both are used on the same workspace or dataset, sensitive content can flow from ms-swift into opik outputs or telemetry. The shared-workspace path is not documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF ms-swift stores tokens, logs, or checkpoints in a workspace that opik can read
IF opik transmits evaluation payloads containing ms-swift artifacts to its backend
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Rotate any hub_token or sdk-token before cross-tool evaluation
Disable upload of raw artifacts in opik where possible
Use a redaction pass on logs and checkpoints before transfer
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate service accounts and storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; opik can send data over a REST API with broad egress. Their write surfaces overlap on shared mutable artifacts even though git locking is not involved. Because no shared-state model is stated, the conflict is plausible but not proven, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or artifact directory
IF opik writes evaluation results back into files that ms-swift also mutates
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent runs on the same dataset
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can generate training/evaluation outputs and opik is an observability/evaluation tool that can act on those outputs. If opik treats ms-swift artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect reports or downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer reading is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF opik renders or forwards ms-swift outputs without independent validation
IF ms-swift-generated metrics are used to trigger automated evaluation or alerting
mitigations: Require a human check before opik publishes ms-swift-derived results
Compare outputs against a second source before actioning them
Mark ms-swift artifacts as untrusted in opik
requires-engineering: add schema validation and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data, while opik is an observability/evaluation service with broad network egress. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch for the same data class. No residency or retention controls are documented for either agent, so the compliance risk is medium, not low.
conditions: IF ms-swift logs or checkpoints contain regulated or customer data
IF opik retains uploaded evaluation traces longer than the source system allows
mitigations: Review what data opik stores before uploading
Redact customer data from ms-swift logs and checkpoints
Set the shortest practical retention window in opik
Export and delete any uploaded traces after review
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency mapping
